previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening dyspnea, found to have acute renal failure, hypercalcemia, and an elevated INR of 16. The hypercalcemia, secondary to multiple myeloma progression, was treated with IV fluids, pamidronate, calcitonin, and steroids, leading to subsequent hypocalcemia managed with aggressive calcium and vitamin D repletion. His renal function improved with hydration, and Coumadin was held then restarted after INR normalization with FFP and vitamin K. A urinary tract infection with Enterococcus was treated with antibiotics. His respiratory symptoms resolved with a course of vancomycin, cefepime, and azithromycin, supported by improving CT findings. Revlimid was resumed as renal function recovered. He was discharged home ambulatory with plans for close outpatient follow-up for calcium monitoring, oncology care, and anticoagulation management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with history of MM s/p autologous stem cell transplant 
in ___ and recent recurrence treated with a 28 day course of 
revlimid who presents from clinic with low grade temp, lethargy, 
suprapubic pain and cough with white sputum. 

# UTI: Found to have dirty UA (but that's his baseline as he has 
a neobladder due to bladder CA), UCx grew VRE (similar to 
before). Treated with daptomycin and discharged on course of 
linezolid. No other source for infection and has been afebrile 
and asx since admission.

# Fevers: Patient presented from clinic with low grade 
temperatures at home up to 99.2 and feeling of general malaise. 
A UA was done on admission and this revealed a WBC of 402 and 
few bacteria. It was initially unclear if this represented a UTI 
as patient has a neobladder and known asymptomatic bacteriuria, 
with VRE, and leukouria. He was started on ciprofloxacin and 
daptomycin empircally as his last UCx had revealed daptomycin 
sensitive VRE. The patient's condition improved on this 
medications and did not have any more significant fevers.

# Atrial fibrillation/flutter: Patient with history of atrial 
fibrillation/flutter. Presents with a subtherapeutic INR at 1.7. 
He was initially continued on his home dose coumadin. INR ranged 
1.8-2.0 in house. Coumadin was not increased as patient's INR 
was likely fluctuating given his changing renal status and 
medication interactions.

# Acute Renal Failure: Patient presented with Cr of 1.4 from a 
baseline of 1.1 on last discharge (___). This was thought to 
be secondary to dehydration from poor po intake as the patient 
had reported. He was given IVF and his renal function improved 
to Cr 1.2.

# Multiple Myeloma: Patient is s/p autologous stem cell 
transplant in ___, known recurrence and recently (course 
finished ___ treated with a 28 day course of revlimid. His 
most recent UPEP showed monoclonal IgG Kappa of 24% (___) up 
from 22% (___) on discharge. 

# Oral ulcers: Patient developed multiple painful oral ulcers 
during his hospitalization. He had previously been treated with 
acyclovir with good response. Acyclovir was started.

# Hypocalcemia: Patient developed hypocalcemia on last admission 
after he was treated for hypercalcemia with pamidronate while he 
had ARF. His calcium level was found to be WNL when corrected 
for albumin.
